content: Brompheniramine is an anticholinergic medication that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of hay fever (allergic rhinitis) and upper respiratory allergies. It is effective in temporarily relieving symptoms such as a runny nose, sneezing, itching of the nose or throat, and itchy, watery eyes. Common side effects include hypersensitivity reactions and drowsiness. This medication is contraindicated in individuals who have a known hypersensitivity to any of its ingredients. Patients with certain medical conditions, such as breathing problems (e.g., emphysema or chronic bronchitis), glaucoma, or difficulty urinating due to an enlarged prostate gland, should consult a doctor before using this medication. Additionally, individuals taking sedatives or tranquilizers should seek medical advice prior to use. When using brompheniramine, drowsiness may occur, and excitability is a potential side effect, particularly in children. Alcohol, sedatives, and tranquilizers can enhance the sedative effects of this medication, so their concurrent use should be avoided. Patients are advised to exercise caution when driving or operating machinery. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using brompheniramine. In the event of an overdose, immediate medical attention or contact with a Poison Control Center is necessary, as overdose symptoms may include hallucinations, convulsions, and potentially fatal outcomes. There is limited information available regarding the use of brompheniramine in pediatric, geriatric, or specific populations such as those with renal or hepatic impairment, immunocompromised patients, or individuals of specific genders or races. Similarly, there is no established guidance on its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, or breastfeeding. Brompheniramine is administered orally, and it is supplied in a tight, light-resistant container with a child-resistant cap. The tablets contain color additives, including FD&C Yellow No. 5 (tartrazine). The recommended storage temperature is between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F). Patients should avoid alcohol while taking brompheniramine, as the interaction between alcohol and this medication has not been fully established. It is important to discuss any potential risks with a healthcare provider.
